extracted.intended_audience: predoctoral fellowship applicants and mentors (NIH F31); NIH peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Summary statement and reviewer critique for an NIH F31 predoctoral fellowship application, using standard fellowship review criteria to evaluate applicant, mentors, research training plan, training potential, and institutional environment. Includes numeric impact score and administrative determinations (human/animal subjects, biohazards, RCR, budget).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant's qualifications, background, productivity, and potential to develop into an independent researcher (examples: undergraduate/graduate record, publications, research experience, perseverance, communication and data management skills).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers list strengths (e.g., excellent preliminary data, publication record, passed qualifying exams, demonstrated commitment, first-generation college student overcoming setbacks) and explicitly note weaknesses when present (many critiques here list 'None noted'). The applicant's potential to become an independent, productive scientist is a core consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsors, Collaborators, and Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the quality, experience, and complementarity of mentors and collaborators, their mentoring track records, relevant expertise, and current funding relevant to the proposed training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers highlighted strengths such as mentors' years of mentoring experience, complementary expertise (structural biology and virology), track records training students who went on to careers, and co-sponsor support. Weaknesses include potential concerns about sponsor's current funding alignment (e.g., sponsor's R01 not directly related to proposed work) mitigated by pending related funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the scientific training plan: clarity of central hypothesis, specificity of aims, feasibility, rigor of approaches, identification of potential pitfalls and alternatives, and degree of risk (e.g., high-risk/high-reward aims; need to learn new techniques).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether aims are well articulated and likely to yield publishable results (notes that Aims 1 and 2.1/2.2 are feasible; Aim 2.3 is higher risk). They comment on feasibility within requested timeframe and note need for significant time to acquire new technical skills (mass spectrometry, X-ray crystallography). The plan should present alternatives and interpretations and a clear path to test hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of how the fellowship will advance the applicant's development toward an independent research career, including planned professional development activities, coursework, teaching, conferences, and skills acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider the applicant's prior experience, proposed training activities (seminars, journal clubs, national/international meetings, teaching assistantship, statistics course), Individual Development Plan (IDP) requirements, and whether the plan is likely to produce growth. Weaknesses include the time required to learn new techniques that could slow progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Environment & Commitment to Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the institutional support, resources, and programmatic commitments that will enable the applicant's training (e.g., availability of equipment, faculty participation, formal programs like IDP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers cite availability of outstanding resources, requirement for an IDP, active seminar/workshop offerings, and faculty involvement as strengths. The institutional environment should provide sustained mentoring opportunities and infrastructure for the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Impact Score
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewers' overall impact assessment summarizing the application's likely influence on the applicant's training and future contributions; assigned a numeric impact score (here: Impact Score: 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative Overall Impact synthesizes enthusiasm for applicant, sponsors, institutional environment, and potential impact. Footnote guidance: the impact/priority score is calculated after discussion by averaging overall scores (1-9) from voting reviewers and multiplying by 10. Some applications may also receive a percentile. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting and are not discussed or calculated into the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination whether human subjects are involved and adequacy of protections when applicable (here: 'Not Applicable (No Human Subjects)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects are involved, reviewers evaluate protections; for applications without human subjects, mark as not applicable. FOIA and confidentiality notices may apply to application materials posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination whether live vertebrate animals are involved and adequacy of animal care and use protections (here: 'Not Applicable (No Vertebrate Animals involved for competing appl.)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, reviewers assess justification for and care of vertebrate animals; otherwise mark not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether proposed research involves biohazards and whether protections and containment plans are acceptable (examples on this application: 'Acceptable' and in other places 'Not Applicable').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers explicitly state whether biohazards are acceptable or not applicable; if biohazards are involved, plans and safety measures must be described and judged acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the adequacy of plans for training in research ethics and responsible conduct (format, subject matter, faculty participation, duration, frequency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required elements include format (face-to-face), subject matter covering appropriate ethics/principles, faculty participation, duration (annual, ongoing workshops), and frequency (e.g., 6- and 8-hour courses, at least four additional workshops, monthly one-hour workshops). Reviewers marked RCR as 'Acceptable' when these components were adequately described. Scientific Review Officer may note RCR adequacy separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans for sharing data, tools, and other resources developed in the project (here: 'Acceptable').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether resource sharing plans meet expectations; acceptable plans are noted as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support / Committee Budget Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation regarding requested budget and project period (committee recommendation: 'Recommend as Requested'; committee budget recommendations are summarized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers/committee recommend funding levels; committee recommendations (e.g., approve requested budget) are recorded. Additional administrative notes may accompany budget recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on RCR Format/Subject Matter/Faculty Participation/Duration/Frequency (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific required commentary items for RCR training format and delivery (enumerated comments: Format, Subject Matter, Faculty Participation, Duration, Frequency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example comments from reviewers: Format — 'Face to face'; Subject Matter — 'Ethics and principles appropriate for research'; Faculty Participation — 'Various faculty' or 'A large number of faculty participate'; Duration — 'Annual' or 'Ongoing seminars...beginning in the first year and continuing through the final years'; Frequency — '6 hour and 8 hour courses' and 'frequency of seminars and workshops throughout the graduate program provides continued exposure... which meets the NIH requirement for retraining every four years.' These detailed comments are required items in fellowship review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative/summary notes prepared by the SRO summarizing committee discussion outcomes or reviewer critiques (example: 'Training in the responsible conduct of research was adequately described').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRO notes capture committee-level administrative summaries such as budget recommendations and clarifications about training adequacy; these supplement individual reviewer critiques and may highlight procedural items (e.g., FOIA, resubmission policy link).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring Process and Policy Footnotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit description of NIH peer review scoring and resubmission policy (example footnote text describing modified policy on resubmissions and how the impact/priority score is calculated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnote text explains: NIH modified policy regarding receipt of resubmissions (see notice NOT-OD-14-074), impact/priority score is calculated by averaging overall scores (1-9) from voting reviewers then multiplying by 10; criterion scores are submitted prior to meeting and not discussed or calculated into overall impact score; some applications receive percentile rankings; links provided for peer review process details.
